- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 10–25% if recent price is trending down.  
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >30% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent high for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), apply mean reversion: subtract 0.1–0.2 from forecast for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is erratic, assume low volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >2.5x recent 18-day average, flag as overconfident; reduce by 30–50% if sentiment is weak or negative.  
- If forecast shows strong downward trend after recent spike, check for sentiment reversal; if sentiment turns positive, reduce downward momentum by 50%.
